events.did: stood before the unlocked metal door that led into EON, expecting death, the doctor, and Sydney beyond it
events.quote_anchor: He knew what lay beyond the threshold. What was waiting for him there.

events.did: drew the inhaler from his coat, held it to the light to study the violet liquid and calculated how much he would need
events.quote_anchor: He held it to the light, studying the violet liquid in the cartridge, calculating how much he’d need.

events.did: asked Victor in his ear if he was ready, and Victor answered that he was
events.quote_anchor: “Hey, Vic,” said a voice in his ear. “Are you ready?”

events.did: pushed open the door and stepped out onto the roof, letting the door smash against the wall
events.quote_anchor: Eli chuckled when the door smacked against the wall, the metal ringing like a bell.

events.did: swore and guided the door shut, because the last thing either of them wanted right now was an audience
events.quote_anchor: The last thing either of them wanted right now was an audience.

events.did: crossed the roof with the grim determination of a penitent, with Victor following, while still wearing the hospital bracelet from his failed transformation
events.quote_anchor: No, this was a private pilgrimage (Eli’s words, of course). He crossed the roof with the grim determination of a penitent

events.did: insisted on going up to see the stars one last time, in case something went wrong, while his bath ice melted downstairs
events.quote_anchor: he’d insisted on seeing the stars one last time, in case something went wrong.

events.did: stopped in the center of the roof, tipped his head back and frowned at the overcast sky
events.quote_anchor: Eli stopped in the center of the roof, hands at his sides as his head tipped back. He frowned.

relations.did: Eli speaks into Victor's ear and Victor's mouth tugs into a grim smile at the path that led them here
relations.quote_anchor: His mouth tugged into a grim smile. Of all the ways this could have gone.

relations.did: the two of them laugh together under the starless sky, and Victor thinks this may be the one moment he would choose to live inside
relations.quote_anchor: He and Eli, laughing beneath a starless, ordinary sky.

relations.did: Eli always puts a lot of stock in the Almighty and would take the overcast sky as a sign of disapproval
relations.quote_anchor: the fact he would probably take it as a sign of disapproval from the Almighty he was always putting so much stock in

relations.did: it is Eli's turn tonight in the bath downstairs, and Victor followed him up to the roof
relations.quote_anchor: It was Eli’s turn tonight, the ice already melting in the bath downstairs

numbers.did: how many stories tall it was: three
numbers.quote_anchor: And they probably would have, but the building was only three stories tall.

numbers.did: how many times the roof door latch had been hacked, picked and forced before facilities gave up
numbers.quote_anchor: But the latch had been hacked at, picked, and forced so many times that facilities finally gave up

numbers.did: the wording of the sign pinned to it: NO ACCESS
numbers.quote_anchor: a stern sign pinned to the door that said NO ACCESS so they’d have plausible deniability

numbers.did: what they brought with them when they flocked to the roof: beers and cigarettes and joints
numbers.quote_anchor: They’d flock, with beers and cigarettes and joints, afraid of missing out on some impromptu gathering.
